original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: In the pinned P112 fixed-reader exact two-total decoder XX^t = XY^t + (XA)Z^t, Y = X - ZA^t (A 8x2, Z 112x2), with deletion union U = supp(z1) u supp(z2) of size at most 48: what is the exact geometric maximum retained loss L(U), what is the maximum retained loss realizable by a rank-two correction ZA^t, and what COPY rank-sum floor follows when both added terms are charged (PR2382 open next question 1, band 48)?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for block-climb decoders; this package answers a concrete, unclaimed open boundary of the complex supplier's P112 decoder COPY bill (PR2382 OQ1, discussion 2369 handoff). It decides whether the separate-total no-saving range extends to source union 48 and records the new loss geometry there.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the complex supplier's P112 decoder COPY bill: a fixed-reader two-total decoder could only lower copied information if its COPY rank sum drops below 64. This package shows that at source union 48 it cannot in the full-rank on-column case (provable lower bound 65; attainment open, the explicit loss-5 witness costs 74), so it is not a route to a new kappa.
stop_rule: Stop once band 48 is closed: complete enumeration of all closed-support configurations plus an exact rank-two necessary condition and an explicit realization proving the stated floor, or an explicit realizable profile with its bill. Bands 49+ out of scope. Hard stop 2026-10-15T15:03:33Z for experiments.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, exact Fraction/F2 arithmetic, ~165 s, peak RSS ~175 MB on CPython 3.14) recomputes all closed supports of the eight reader codes up to size 48, enumerates every retained-loss configuration with union <= 47 and <= 48 by a lead-support case split, applies the rank-two necessary condition to every fully specified column subset, and checks an explicit two-column witness on all 12,544 identity pairs. Results: geometric max L = 5 (<=47, reproducing PR2382) and 8 (48); rank-two retained loss bound 4 (<=47) and 5 (48), the latter attained (bill 74); price minimum 6; full-rank on-column COPY lower bound 66 (unions 44..47) and 65 (48; attainment open, witness bill 74). RESULT.json is compared exactly; four negative controls must be rejected.

open_questions.question: Is the relaxation floor 65 at union 48 attained by an actual decoder, i.e. is there a two-column correction with retained loss 5 whose two added COPY ranks sum to 6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The only explicit loss-5 witness has bill 74; if no loss-5 correction can have a source of at most four active labels, the full-rank floor at 48 is at least 66 and the PR2382 bound extends unchanged.
open_questions.first_step: Shape 4+1 costs >= 66 by a written argument in PROOF.md (12/12 cut sign balance, machine-checked as premise P3, forces >= 12 ports for every nonzero vector of col W; the constrained price minimum 7 is not scripted). For shapes 3+1+1, 2+1+1+1 and 1^5, derive the minimum support of a nonzero vector in col W from their patterns and free entries.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires a joint price/realizability argument (sufficiency of the rank-two completion for each shape is not decided here).

open_questions.question: Do bands 49..51 keep the two-column retained loss at most 6 (COPY >= 64)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would extend the fixed-reader two-total no-saving range beyond 48; geometric losses already reach 8 at 48.
open_questions.first_step: Re-run the lead-support case split with cap 49: no closed supports of size 37..39 exist, so leads with s>36 have s>=40 and stay cut-only; widen the s=36 branch to 13 outside ports and extend the closed-support census past 48.
open_questions.blocked_by: Closed-support enumeration grows quickly above 48; the s=36 branch budget rises to 13.

open_questions.question: Which of the N-passing shapes 3+1+1, 2+1+1+1 and 1^5 at union 48 are actually realizable by a rank-two correction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only 4+1 is realized explicitly; the minor test is necessary, not sufficient. A complete classification would show which loss geometries a two-column decoder can use.
open_questions.first_step: For each shape class, parametrize A (8x2) and solve the per-row linear conditions x_r|K_r in col(A[K_r,:]) exactly.
open_questions.blocked_by: Polynomial feasibility in A; not needed for the floor because 5 is already attained.
